passage: “Ankita, you asked what I did when the bank called, so here it is. I'm Preeti, by the way. A man said my account would be frozen unless I confirmed a code. My hands were sweating, and I kept thinking, what if it's real? But I said, ‘I'll call you back,’ and he gave me a number, and something felt off. So I hung up and did not call it. I found my mother and said, ‘Can you phone the bank on the number printed on your card?’ She did. It took a while on hold. Then the woman at the bank said there was no block on any account, and that they never ask for codes on calls. My mother put her hand on my shoulder. I still felt a bit shaky.”

qa.q: Whose number did Preeti's mother phone the bank on?
qa.a: The number printed on her card.

qa.q: How did Preeti feel while the call was happening?
qa.a: Anxious: Preeti's hands were sweating and Preeti kept thinking it might be real, yet chose to check instead of trusting the number.

qa.q: What else could Preeti do after learning it was fake, and why?
qa.a: Tell other family members and report the number, since scammers try the same script on many people.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Preeti's mother?
qa.a: Preeti's mother gets a straight answer from the bank on the official number and sees that Preeti was careful, which is reassuring.

grounding: A student ends the call, does not use the number given and has the mother phone the bank on the card number, learning no block exists.

passage:
I'm Kamal, and I was doing homework on the sofa when my sister Chandrika's phone rang. She put it on speaker by mistake. A man said there was a problem with Amma's bank card and she had to call back, quickly, on a number he'd text, before it got blocked.
Chandrika said, “Okay, thank you,” and ended the call. The text with the number came a minute later. She didn't touch it. She went to the kitchen, where Amma was chopping onions, and asked for Amma's wallet.
They took out the card and turned it over. Amma dialled the helpline printed on the back, not the one in the text. I heard Amma say, “No block? Nothing?” She was quiet for a bit after that, then hugged Chandrika with onion hands.
I don't know if Chandrika was scared. She looked very calm. Maybe too calm.

qa.a: The helpline printed on the back of the card, not the one in the text.

qa.q: What might Chandrika have been feeling, going by what Kamal saw?
qa.a: She may have been scared underneath, but she looked calm and in control, choosing not to touch the texted number.

qa.q: What else could the family do after learning there was no block?
qa.a: Report the caller's number to the bank and block it on the phone, so it cannot be used on them or anyone else again.

qa.q: What was the moment like for Amma?
qa.a: Amma, quiet and then hugging Chandrika, was probably shaken by how close it came and relieved the card was safe.

grounding: A sibling watches a student end a scam call, ignore the number given, and have her mother call the bank using the number on the card.
